mbm-0293.clue: We gave the last move a different name.
mbm-0293.quote: There’s a point on our climbing wall where I used to say I’m stuck. My friend started calling it the balcony. Now I stop there, look out over the gym and enjoy the view before I reach up.

mbm-0294.quote: One white stone in our baduk set rings much brighter than the rest. My grandfather kept it till the end of the game. I still do, even if I’m a hundred moves behind.

mbm-0295.clue: My skis go quiet in the orange light.
mbm-0295.quote: At sunset I like the easy run past the lodge windows. Each pane flashes orange as I glide by. By the time I’m at the bottom I’ve lit the whole building.

mbm-0296.clue: Let me straighten the little rake.
mbm-0296.quote: I missed a bunker shot three times. Afterwards I raked the sand into a tidy fan that looked just like the sunrise. My next shot was better, but the raking was my favorite stroke.

mbm-0297.clue: My museum pass has a paw on it.
mbm-0297.quote: I sketched a fossil footprint on the back while waiting for the rain to stop. My dog put a muddy paw beside it that evening. I’ve been showing people my two-species collection ever since.

mbm-0298.clue: I’ve got half a picture of a birthday cake.
mbm-0298.quote: My nephew leaned in so close to blow the candles that his ear landed right in the middle of the frame. The candles lit up his whole cheek. That one went straight in the family album.

mbm-0299.clue: My scissors stay sharp for the feathers.
mbm-0299.quote: I cut quetzals from folded green tissue to hang across our patio. One wing came out shorter than the other and the bird kept turning in the breeze. It was the only one that seemed to dance.

mbm-0300.clue: My favorite line has three words.
mbm-0300.quote: I play the porter in our mystery show. I only say the train’s late. Last night a real train blew its whistle outside right afterwards. Nobody in the audience believed we hadn’t arranged it.

mbm-0301.clue: We dress for the weather report.
mbm-0301.quote: On our Friday pajama nights we put on scarves when the weather reporter says snow. Halfway through the July reruns it got pretty warm in that living room. Rules are rules in my sister’s house.

mbm-0302.clue: I keep a towel on the porch rail.
mbm-0302.quote: I practiced getting up on water skis for a week and swallowed half the lake. On the day I stayed up, my family waved that enormous striped towel from shore. I could see it all the way round the bay.

mbm-0303.clue: Take the spoon out of the drawer first.
mbm-0303.quote: I practice my coin trick over the cutlery drawer so anything I drop lands somewhere interesting. I once lost a coin in a ladle and discovered a much better ending.

mbm-0304.clue: I never wash the chalk off that corner.
mbm-0304.quote: We marked the turn in my kata with a bit of chalk on the floor. When I finally got it right my teacher drew a little flower there. We wipe round it when we clean the room.

mbm-0305.clue: The tiny flowers are for turning.
mbm-0305.quote: My aunt let me embroider a line of buds on the hem of her pollera. When she spun in the courtyard the buds seemed to open all at once. I had never seen my stitches move before.

mbm-0306.clue: The first thing I heard back on the ground was a zip.
mbm-0306.quote: After my jump we spread the canopy out like a second sky. My little brother zipped up his jacket and asked if he could help fold a cloud. I saved him a corner.

mbm-0307.clue: That bus map isn’t the book’s map.
mbm-0307.quote: The fantasy novel I bought secondhand was missing its map. I drew a kingdom using our bus routes. The royal castle is the last stop on the number four, just past my dentist.

mbm-0308.clue: Here’s why I buy the soft onions.
mbm-0308.quote: I juggled three onions at our market stall to make my niece laugh. One landed in the weighing pan and the needle stopped dead on one pound. Now customers ask for the flying measure.

mbm-0309.clue: We take the lane by the window.
mbm-0309.quote: A sparrow comes to the window at the far end of our indoor pool. I do a lap, look up, and there it is again. It’s the only spectator who’s never asked me my time.

mbm-0310.clue: Our trail lunch has a roof you can eat.
mbm-0310.quote: I hollowed out a little loaf and packed cheese inside for a hike. We sat above the valley and lifted the crust like a cottage roof. My friend still asks if lunch has a chimney.

mbm-0311.clue: Stand where the blue tile is.
mbm-0311.quote: I painted our courtyard on a little wooden box, lining up the arch on the lid with the real one. From the blue tile by the drain you can hold it up and the street fits together.

mbm-0312.clue: The quilt has a crease where the letter folds.
mbm-0312.quote: I copied an old airmail envelope in blue cloth and red stitches. My cousin uses it on the guest bed. She says everyone who sleeps there has arrived by special delivery.

mbm-0313.clue: I put a window in the heel.
mbm-0313.quote: I built a tiny repair bay into the heel of my model robot. You have to turn it over to see the mechanic’s yellow chair. The other club members spend more time looking at its feet than its face.

mbm-0314.clue: I save money on the interval snacks.
mbm-0314.quote: I bring my own popcorn and swap it with my friend for one of his lime sweets. We’ve been doing it since our first double feature. He still waits for the lights to go down to make the trade.

mbm-0315.clue: The thread changes color halfway through.
mbm-0315.quote: I had just enough black thread for one seam and green for the other. I used both inside my winter coat. When I hang it up inside out it looks as if spring is arriving from the left.

mbm-0316.clue: The extra ribbon stays in my pocket.
mbm-0316.quote: At our outdoor folk dance the ribbon on an old man’s shoe came loose. We tied on my spare with the music still going. The circle came round again just in time for us to join.

mbm-0317.clue: That chip on the wall marks our best shot.
mbm-0317.quote: My grandmother’s bocce ball kissed the wall, rolled past three of ours and stopped against the little target. She put a flowerpot below the chip. We’ve watered that victory all summer.
